html:
The Coos, Lower Umpqua and Siuslaw are three Native American peoples of the central Oregon coast, around Coos Bay and the mouths of the Umpqua and Siuslaw rivers. Today they form one tribe, the Confederated Tribes of Coos, Lower Umpqua and Siuslaw Indians.

They lived in plank house villages on bays and estuaries, from fish, shellfish, seals and berries. In 1855 their leaders signed a treaty giving up their land, but the US Senate never ratified it. They were nevertheless moved, and many were held at Fort Umpqua and then at the Yachats reservation, where many died. In 1954 the US ended its recognition of them under the termination policy; it was restored in 1984. Their neighbours include the Coquille, the Alsea and the Tututni.
